subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool silently corrupts 2>&1 / 2>/dev/null shell redirect arguments

question: Should maintainers keep this issue waiting for a current-main reproduction/log payload, or close it as no longer reproducible from the inspected exec and Codex paths?
rationale: Current main source and tests preserve redirect text, but the shipped report is concrete enough that closing without the missing payload boundary would be premature.

options.title: Keep for targeted repro
options.body: Ask for or run a current-main reproduction that captures the raw tool call arguments before and after OpenClaw normalization, then route the fix to the proven boundary.

options.title: Close as unreproduced
options.body: Close if maintainers decide the inspected current-main paths and existing tests are sufficient proof that the 2026.5.27 behavior no longer applies.

recommendation.title: Keep for targeted repro
recommendation.body: Ask for or run a current-main reproduction that captures the raw tool call arguments before and after OpenClaw normalization, then route the fix to the proven boundary.
